newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa warns Boeing on future procurement.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa warns Boeing on future procurement.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG warned Thursday that its future procurement of aircraft from Boeing Co. could be affected by the U.S. aircraft manufacturer's plans to enter airline maintenance.
A Lufthansa spokesman confirmed comments made by Chairman Juergen Weber in the German business daily Handelsblatt describing any such a move by Boeing as "bad business behavior."
Lufthansa, which has purchased around half of its fleet from Seattle-based Boeing, is also a world leader in jet maintenance, particularly outside the United States.
"If Boeing sets up in competition to us, it will have an impact on our future procurement. After all, we don't build airplanes," Weber was quoted as telling journalists in New York.
The Lufthansa spokesman confirmed that a reduction in future purchases from the U.S. planemaker was a possible outcome of Boeing's decision to enter aircraft maintenance.
Boeing confirmed this month that it was considering taking over maintenance operations for some of its airline customers as part of a diversification drive.

Nancy Bethel, vice president for customers in Boeing's commercial airplane group, acknowledged the manufacturer is walking "a very fine line" in its exploration of opportunities in the maintenance business.
But she said in an interview that while some of Boeing's airline customers have profitable maintenance operations, others are "begging for us to get into the maintenance market."
A spokewoman for Boeing Enterprises, the new company unit exploring a possible maintenance venture, said the area was only one of many being explored and that no decisions had been made.
"We certainly do not want to do anything that would compromise our positive, long-standing relationships with any of our customers," said the spokeswoman, Barbara Murphy.
Lufthansa Technik, Lufthansa's maintenance division, contributed third-quarter pre-tax profits of 44 million marks ($25.6 million), around a 10th of the group's total.

Weber also hit out at "exclusive provider" relationships recently forged between Boeing and airlines such as AMR Corp.'s American Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc., saying Lufthansa would never enter such an arrangement.
"We shall continue to buy the best airplanes at the most favorable prices," he was quoted as saying.
